facts: component_legend_as_printed

Figure legend labels (not quantities): 1: Motherboard; 2: Low-profile PCIe cards; 3: Power supplies; 4: Power supply backplane; 5: Drive backplane; 6: System lithium battery; 7: CPUs and heatsinks; 8: Memory risers; 9: Fan board; 10: Fan modules; 11: Boot drives and SSDs. service_restriction_as_printed
Field-replaceable units should only be replaced by trained Oracle service technicians. [HTML #ZFSRE-GUID-23D9E421-97EA-4692-B197-0F5E78A142A3; article paragraphs 14]
power_description

SP subsystem controls host power and monitors host events. SP controller uses host 3.3V standby rail whenever AC input is present, even when system is off. [HTML #ZFSRE-GUID-23D9E421-97EA-4692-B197-0F5E78A142A3; article paragraphs 15]
power_description

Power Distribution Board is a FRU: distributes main 12V from supplies; connects to Vertical PDB, motherboard bus bar/ribbon cable and top-cover interlock kill switch. power supplies → power supply backplane → power distribution board topology is explicitly described. [HTML #ZFSRE-GUID-23D9E421-97EA-4692-B197-0F5E78A142A3; article paragraphs 16]
physical_description

Vertical PDB Card, also called vertical power distribution board or Paddle Card, is a FRU interconnecting PDB with fan power boards, hard-drive backplane and I/O board. [HTML #ZFSRE-GUID-23D9E421-97EA-4692-B197-0F5E78A142A3; article paragraphs 17]
power_description

Power Supply Backplane Card connects the PDB to power supplies 0 and 1. These are named connection positions; no PSU model, rating or redundancy inference is supplied. [HTML #ZFSRE-GUID-23D9E421-97EA-4692-B197-0F5E78A142A3; article paragraphs 18]
cooling_description

Two fan power boards are FRUs; power fan modules, carry status LEDs and transfer I2C fan-module data. Two refers to boards, not fan-module quantity. [HTML #ZFSRE-GUID-23D9E421-97EA-4692-B197-0F5E78A142A3; article paragraphs 19]
physical_description

Six-drive backplane is a FRU with drive connectors, I/O-board interconnect, Power/Locator buttons and status LEDs; this is not an installed-drive count. [HTML #ZFSRE-GUID-23D9E421-97EA-4692-B197-0F5E78A142A3; article paragraphs 20]
physical_description

Documented configuration/cluster rule in dated OS8.8.x manual, not installed-unit inventory: Two system boot drives in slots 0 and 1 form a mirrored pair; up to four read-optimized cache SSDs can populate slots 2–5 in order. In a Sun ZFS Storage 7420 clustered configuration, both controllers SSD counts must match. [HTML #ZFSRE-GUID-23D9E421-97EA-4692-B197-0F5E78A142A3; article paragraphs 22]
cooling_description

Fan-module fault indications: front/rear Service Action Required LEDs, front Fan Module Service Action Required (TOP) LED, and Fan Fault LED on/adjacent to faulty module. System Overtemp LED might also light if temperature rises. [HTML #ZFSRE-GUID-23D9E421-97EA-4692-B197-0F5E78A142A3; article paragraphs 37,39,40,41,42]

Sun ZFS Storage 7420 Internal Boards - The Sun ZFS Storage 7420 controller chassis has the following boards installed. Field-replaceable units (FRUs) should only be replaced by trained Oracle service technicians.

Motherboard: The motherboard is a FRU and includes CPU modules, slots for eight DIMM risers, memory control subsystems, and the service processor (SP) subsystem. The SP subsystem controls the host power and monitors host system events (power and environmental). The SP controller draws power from the host's 3.3V standby supply rail, which is available whenever the system is receiving AC input power, even when the system is turned off.

Power Distribution Board: The power distribution board is a FRU and distributes main 12V power from the power supplies to the rest of the system. It is directly connected to the Vertical PDB card, and to the motherboard through a bus bar and ribbon cable. It also supports a top cover interlock ("kill") switch. In the storage controller, the power supplies connect to the power supply backplane which connects to the power distribution board.

Vertical PDB Card: The vertical power distribution board, or Paddle Card is a FRU and serves as the interconnect between the power distribution board and the fan power boards, hard drive backplane, and I/O board.
Power Supply Backplane Card: This board connects the power distribution board to power supplies 0 and 1.
Fan Power Boards: The two fan power boards are FRUs and carry power to the storage controller fan modules. In addition, they contain fan module status LEDs and transfer I2C data for the fan modules.

Drive Backplane: The six-drive backplane is a FRU and includes the connectors for the drives, as well as the interconnect for the I/O board, Power and Locator buttons, and system/component status LEDs. Each drive has an LED indicator for Power/Activity, Fault, and Locate.

Sun ZFS Storage 7420 controllers have two system boot drives in slots 0 and 1, configured as a mirrored pair. Up to four read-optimized cache SSDs, may fill slots 2 through 5, in order. In a Sun ZFS Storage 7420 clustered configuration, the number of SSDs installed in both controllers must match.

Sun ZFS Storage 7420 Fan Modules - The Fan Modules and Fan Module LEDs of the Sun ZFS Storage 7420 controller are shown in the following figure. The following LEDs are lit when a fan module fault is detected:
Front and rear Service Action Required LEDs
Fan Module Service Action Required (TOP) LED on the front of the controller
Fan Fault LED on or adjacent to the faulty fan module
The system Overtemp LED might light if a fan fault causes an increase in system operating temperature.

devices.title: Sun ZFS Storage 7420
facts: physical_description

Attached storage: one to six chains; each chain contains up to six HDD-only or SSD-capable disk shelves, combined in any order. No shelf/cable model or wiring topology is stated here. [HTML #ZFSRE-GUID-6D3F47EA-7D39-46CC-B484-3CC3BF6671DB; article paragraphs 1]

source_text: Primary storage for Sun ZFS Storage 7420 controllers is provided by one to six chains of attached storage. Each chain consists of up to six HDD-only or SSD-capable disk shelves, combined in any order. For more information, see Connecting to Attached Storage . See also Disk Shelf Hardware Overview for component specifications and diagrams.
